paras: The whitecapping of George Davis was an attack on a Black mail carrier on the route between Bogue Chitto and Ambler, Mississippi, whose house was fired into by white men who threatened to kill him unless he quit carrying the mail, as reported in 1905. A federal grand jury indicted four men, and two of them, Douglass Holloway and John Ratliff, were brought in by United States marshals and released on bond.

Davis, described as "a negro mail carrier," carried the mail between Bogue Chitto and Ambler, and the item reporting the case was headed "Two Lincoln Whitecappers," placing the accused in Lincoln County.

The men were alleged to have fired into the mail carrier's house and to have threatened to kill him if he did not quit carrying the mail over that route. No date for the shooting is given, and no injury to Davis or anyone in the house is reported.

The case went before a federal grand jury, which indicted four men for interfering with and "bulldozing" him. United States Marshals W. O. Ligon and Edgar S. Wilson, Jr. came in from Bogue Chitto with Holloway and Ratliff, described as "two white men"; the other two indicted men had not been arrested. Arraigned before Commissioner Moseley, the pair waived examination and were placed under bond of $1,000 each to appear at the next session of federal court.
No report of a trial or verdict was found in the coverage.

The only known account is a short item from the Jackson Clarion-Ledger, reprinted on August 2, 1905, on page 3 of The Leader of Brookhaven. Its headline, "Two Lincoln Whitecappers. Charged with Interfering with a Negro Mail Carrier," named the accused as whitecappers, and the text presented the shooting and threat as allegations without editorial comment. No other report of the case, in either the white or the Black press, appears in the coverage.
